name: Galactus DB
tagline: Rust graph database speaking Cypher over Bolt, with SQL tables and vector search in the same engine.
description: Galactus DB is a property-graph database written in Rust that speaks Cypher over the Bolt protocol, so the official Neo4j drivers connect and Neo4j 4.x and 5.x dump files import directly. A node property can hold a typed table that is queried and changed with SQL (joins, window functions, recursive CTEs) inside a Cypher statement and the same transaction as the graph. Vector, full-text and spatial indexes, GDS-style graph algorithms, APOC utilities, change streams and an MCP server for AI agents are built in. It ships as a container image of about 5 MB for Linux AMD64 and ARM64. Each instance runs on one server with replicas for reads; the free Community edition is licensed for production use, with Commercial and Enterprise sold per core.

license.name: Proprietary (free Community edition; Commercial and Enterprise per core)

pricing.notes: Community is free for any use, including production, with up to three active user databases. Commercial adds unlimited databases and backup/restore, with term or perpetual licences per core. Enterprise adds replicas on other servers and support.

scale.notes: One server per instance; graph structure and indexes are held in memory with properties paged from disk. Read-only replicas can run on the same or another server (Enterprise). A cluster edition with property sharding is in early access.

strengths: Typed SQL tables on nodes and relationships, queried with SQL (joins, window functions, recursive CTEs) inside Cypher in the same transaction
GIS built in: WGS-84 points plus geometry and geography shapes from WKT, WKB and GeoJSON, with spatial indexes and shortest-path routing
Nebula Cluster (early access) adds high availability with automatic failover; apps keep their Bolt driver and bolt:// address
Vector search, FastRP embeddings and an MCP server for GraphRAG and AI agents, all in the same engine as the graph
Bolt and Cypher: official Neo4j drivers connect, and Neo4j 4.x/5.x .dump files import without a Neo4j install
Built-in GDS-style algorithms, APOC utilities, change streams and a constraint-based scheduler (gdb.schedule)
Container image of about 5 MB for Linux AMD64 and ARM64; the free Community edition runs in production with no licence key
weaknesses: The server is closed source; only the drivers are open source (Apache-2.0)
Young project with a small community and few third-party tools beyond the Neo4j ecosystem
Released instances scale up, not out: the cluster edition is in early access
useCases: Knowledge graphs combining graph structure with tabular records
Route finding and shortest paths on road networks
Scheduling and resource planning on graph data
Moving existing Neo4j applications to a smaller footprint
notIdealFor: Graphs that must be sharded across many machines today
Teams that require an open-source server
